blocks.content: A judge of the Supreme Court can be removed from office only by an order of the President passed after an address by each House of Parliament supported by a special majority.

rows: Same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge
No grounds specified in the Constitution

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Judges of the Supreme Court hold office until attaining the age of 65 years and submit their resignation directly to the President.
The removal of a Supreme Court Judge requires a special majority in both Houses of Parliament on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity under Article 124(4).
The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) and Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) are removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court Judge.
UPSC Chairman and members serve for 6 years or until 65 years of age, and can be removed by the President only after an inquiry by the Supreme Court.
The President resigns by writing to the Vice-President, whereas the Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President without fixed security of tenure.
The phrase 'violation of the Constitution' is the sole ground for impeachment of the President under Article 61, but it is not explicitly defined in the Constitution.
The resignation letter of the President is addressed to the Vice-President, who must forthwith communicate it to the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
The Constitution does not lay down any specific grounds or procedure for the removal of a State Governor by the President.
CAG and CEC cannot be removed except on the same grounds and in the same manner as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
